clue.text: Rail transport for the lower classes?

definitions.text: Rail transport for the lower classes?

parts.words: Rail transport for the lower classes?
parts.note: reads like a railway carriage for poorer passengers, but the lower classes are livestock, and the joke is the slang 'cattle class' for cramped cheap travel

explanation.surface: A sneer at how a rail operator packs in its cheapest passengers.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway wagon built to carry livestock, with a dig at cheap, crowded passenger travel.

clue.text: Raised protection from wet in river

indicators.note: in a down entry raising a word lifts it so it reads from bottom upwards

parts.note: a mac, mackintosh, is a raincoat

explanation.surface: Someone holds a waterproof up while in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cam is the river flowing through Cambridge.

clue.text: Belief one's brought up not to change

indicators.note: in a down entry, bringing the word up reverses it, and it stays the same, so it reads identically both ways

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A principle someone was raised never to abandon.
explanation.walkthrough: The word read upwards is still itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A principle or doctrine held to be true.

clue.text: Lure fish over on one side of boat

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning over makes the pieces read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to draw is to attract or lure
an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: An angler tempts fish from over the side of a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses the whole run DRAWEEL.
explanation.definitionFit: The sheltered side of a vessel, away from the wind.

clue.text: Proper conduct in China is put to every head of government

parts.note: Tao is the Chinese idea of the right way or path of conduct
each means every

explanation.surface: Chinese etiquette is recommended to all national leaders.
explanation.walkthrough: The Taoiseach is the prime minister of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish prime minister, leader of the government of Ireland.

clue.text: Fanatic's extremely useful technique picked up

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters, taken from useful
in a down entry, picking a word up turns it to read bottom to top

parts.note: art means skill or technique

explanation.surface: A zealot's handy method is adopted by others.
explanation.definitionFit: An extremist, someone holding radical views.

clue.text: Ready, we hear, to have border moved to North in divided province

indicators.note: says the word for ready is heard, so it is spelt by sound

parts.note: ready money is cash

indicators.note: in a down entry, going north means reading upwards

parts.note: a rim is an edge or border

explanation.surface: A territory split between nations finds its frontier shifted northwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready' is cash, as in 'the ready'.
explanation.definitionFit: Kashmir is the region split between India, Pakistan and China.

clue.text: Extra material I put on letter

parts.note: PS, a postscript, is extra material added at the foot of a letter

explanation.surface: Someone adds a postscript and signs off with 'I' on a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letter' looks like the correspondence the PS belongs to, but it is the Greek letter being defined.
explanation.definitionFit: Psi is the twenty-third character of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: By which pair got, say, girl?

definitions.text: By which pair got, say, girl?

parts.words: By which pair got, say, girl?
parts.note: reads like asking how a couple obtained a daughter: the means is a woman carrying a baby

explanation.surface: Someone asks how a couple ended up with a daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: The state of carrying a baby before birth, how a couple comes to have a child.

clue.text: Shaking tin, very empty, in the bloody tube?

indicators.note: shaking scrambles the letters of the word tin

parts.note: ravenous means starving, with a very empty stomach

explanation.surface: Someone shakes a tin with nothing in it, in a gory tube.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shaking' turns TIN into INT. The definition is playful: the tube is a vein.
explanation.definitionFit: Into a vein, as an injection or drip; a vein is a blood-filled tube.

clue.text: Chap ordered to leave greens

parts.note: a chap is a man
'Get out!' is the order telling someone to leave

explanation.surface: A man is told to stop eating his vegetables and go.
explanation.definitionFit: Mangetout are flat pea pods eaten whole, a green vegetable.

clue.text: Exhausted, yet excited to be filled with power

indicators.note: the word for excited is a container that has the power symbol placed inside it

parts.note: sent is slang for thrilled or excited, as by music
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: Someone is worn out yet still buzzing with energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Used up, with nothing left: a synonym for drained or worn out.

clue.text: Hit show goes on to gross fortune for them?

definitions.text: Hit show goes on to gross fortune for them?

indicators.note: the show's name follows on after the word for gross, so it is placed second

parts.note: gross can mean fat or overweight
Cats is the long-running hit musical

explanation.surface: A smash musical piles up a vast fortune for its backers.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: wealthy backers who rake in a gross fortune are the very people meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Rich, powerful people, especially executives who collect huge earnings.

clue.text: Brandy and short fizzy drink succeeded as culinary additive

parts.note: fine is French brandy

indicators.note: short means trimmed, so the last letter of the drink is cut

parts.note: sherbet is a fizzy drink or powder
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies

explanation.surface: A cocktail of brandy and pop has worked well as a cooking ingredient.
explanation.definitionFit: A mixture of fresh chopped herbs used as seasoning in French cookery.

clue.text: Country folk burst into song

indicators.note: the word for folk breaks into the word for song, landing inside it

parts.note: an aria is a song in an opera
folk, meaning people, gives men

explanation.surface: Rural singers suddenly start singing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country folk' reads as one phrase about rural people, but 'Country' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A nation in the Caucasus, south of Georgia.

clue.text: Took a minute to become famous.

definitions.meaning: took down a record of a meeting, or wrote a note, as a minute-taker does

explanation.definitionFit: Recorded in writing, and also celebrated or well known: two senses of one past participle.

clue.text: "Depravity" is rude — put it differently

indicators.note: putting letters differently means rearranging them

explanation.surface: A complaint that a word sounds coarse and should be rephrased.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is the link between definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Wickedness, moral corruption.

clue.text: As curse, an awful word

indicators.note: something awful is a mess, so the letters of the preceding words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone recoils at a swear word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As' is kept as it stands at the front, and 'awful' scrambles only what follows. The definition is 'word' in the sense of a promise, as in 'you have my word'.
explanation.definitionFit: A promise or guarantee, as when one gives one's word.

clue.text: Rising current interrupts water sport

indicators.note: the current breaks into the sport's word, sitting inside it

parts.note: surfing is a water sport
AC is alternating current

explanation.surface: An undertow breaks up a session on the waves.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming up to the top, emerging from below water.

clue.text: One feeling sick after the way one's carried in ambulance

indicators.note: the sick person follows the abbreviation for the way, so comes second

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way
a retcher is someone heaving with nausea

explanation.surface: A nauseous patient is being taken to hospital in an ambulance.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the definition as 'what one is carried in' in an ambulance.
explanation.definitionFit: A portable frame or litter on which a patient is carried.

clue.text: Glorious day and night at the theatre

definitions.meaning: the Glorious ... is 12 August, start of the British grouse-shooting season

explanation.definitionFit: The ordinal following eleventh, completing both 'the Glorious ...' and Shakespeare's '... Night'.

clue.text: Authority is silent?

parts.note: being silent is saying nothing, read as says plus O, the figure nought for nothing
being silent is saying nothing, read as says plus O, the figure nought for nothing

explanation.surface: A question whether power lies in keeping quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful reading: one who is silent says nothing, and O stands for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Permission or command: having the final word on whether something happens.

clue.text: Beef from both flanks, and duck, I consumed in greed, perhaps

indicators.note: the pieces are swallowed by the word for greed, placed inside it

parts.note: greed is one of the seven deadly sins
the right and left sides give R and L
a duck is a nought, O, in cricket

explanation.surface: A gluttonous diner eats beef from every side, and duck too.
explanation.walkthrough: The insertion goes after SIN's own I.
explanation.definitionFit: A prime cut from the loin of a cow.

clue.text: Demanding leave to swallow dope

indicators.note: the word for leave takes the word for dope inside it, as if swallowing it

parts.note: to exit is to leave
gen is British slang for information, as is dope

explanation.surface: Someone insists on being allowed off to take drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dope' is information, not a drug: GEN is British slang for the facts.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressing or urgent, requiring much effort or attention.

clue.text: Bear with male that represents family

parts.note: to tote is to carry or bear

explanation.surface: A bear and a male animal stand for a clan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear' is a verb, carry, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: An emblem, often an animal carving, standing for a clan or tribe.

clue.text: Old cow wastes our cash

indicators.note: to waste is to ruin, so the letters of the following words are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A grumble that some old woman squanders the family money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old cow' looks like an insult for a woman, but is literal: an extinct wild ox.
explanation.definitionFit: The aurochs is the extinct wild ox, ancestor of domestic cattle.

clue.text: Marx, as seen in smart circle

parts.note: chic means stylish or smart
O is circle-shaped

explanation.surface: A Marx is spotted in a fashionable set.
explanation.definitionFit: Chico was one of the Marx Brothers comedy team.

clue.text: Left naked? Brazen it out

annotationWithheld.why: Left naked? Brazen it out (5): BLUFF is L inside BUFF (naked), but no word signals the insertion; 'naked' would have to be both BUFF and the container indicator ('in the buff').

clue.text: Quality of clothes in career at sea initially moved one ahead

indicators.note: the opening letter is advanced one step through the alphabet, so the first letter becomes the next one

parts.note: sailoring is the life or work of a sailor

explanation.surface: Someone at sea finds their wardrobe pushing them forward in their naval career.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letter S moves one place on in the alphabet, to T.
explanation.definitionFit: The cut and making of garments, which decides how well clothes fit and hang.

clue.text: Vigour lacking to theatrical veteran

indicators.note: lacking means the word to is removed from the word for vigour

parts.note: gusto is energy or vigour

explanation.surface: An old stage performer has lost his zest.
explanation.walkthrough: Gus is T. S. Eliot's Theatre Cat, an aged actor in Old Possum's poems.
explanation.definitionFit: Gus the Theatre Cat is the elderly actor-cat in T. S. Eliot's poems.

clue.text: Novel ingredient of 11dn

indicators.note: an ingredient is something contained within a mixture, so the letters lie inside the cross-referenced entry

parts.note: 11 down is the herb mixture, fines herbes
the opening stretch of the herb phrase is discarded
the closing stretch of the herb phrase is discarded

explanation.surface: A new component of a herb blend.
explanation.walkthrough: The page printed '11dn', a cross-reference to the herb mixture; the answer sits inside that phrase. 'Novel' is the noun: H. Rider Haggard's 1887 book.
explanation.definitionFit: 'She' is the 1887 adventure novel by H. Rider Haggard.

clue.text: Man runs out of large-size uniform

parts.note: Homo is the human genus, mankind

indicators.note: the runs letter is taken out of the word for large-size

parts.note: a generous portion is large
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A man has run out of uniforms in a big size.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uniform' is the adjective meaning the same throughout, not the clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Alike throughout, of a single consistent kind.
